dialogue.content: （本日は宜しくお願い致します。お時間になりましたら はじめさせていただきます。）
dialogue.English: (Thank you for joining me today. We will begin at the scheduled time.)

dialogue.content: （こちらこそ、よろしくお願い致します）
dialogue.English: (Thank you as well. I look forward to our session.)

dialogue.content: こんにちは！相談員です。本日はお越しいただきありがとうございます。初めに年齢と性別を教えてください。
dialogue.English: Hello! I'm your counselor. Thank you for coming in today. To start, could you please tell me your age and gender?

dialogue.content: 15歳の女性です
dialogue.English: I'm a 15-year-old female.

dialogue.content: 教えてくださりありがとうございます。本日はどのような事をお話しされたいですか？
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing that. What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.content: お母さんのこと
dialogue.English: About my mom.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。お母さんの事でお悩みなんですね。
dialogue.English: I see. You're having some trouble regarding your mother.

dialogue.content: そうだよ
dialogue.English: That's right.

dialogue.content: ええ、毎日顔を合わすご家族のことだからモヤモヤしそうですね。。具体的にはどんなことで悩んだり、考えたりしていますか？
dialogue.English: Yes, I can imagine it must be frustrating when it's about a family member you see every day. Specifically, what kind of things have been bothering you or on your mind?

dialogue.content: いちいち口出ししてうるさいの
dialogue.English: She's always nagging me about every little thing.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね、、　いちいち言われたら嫌な気分になっちゃいますね。よければどんなことにを言うのか、言える範囲で教えてくれますか？
dialogue.English: I see... It must be unpleasant to be nagged about every little thing. If you're comfortable, could you tell me what kinds of things she says, within the scope of what you're willing to share?

dialogue.content: 勉強しろっていう
dialogue.English: She tells me to study.

dialogue.content: そうか、勉強しろって・・・
dialogue.English: I see, she tells you to study...

dialogue.content: イライラしちゃいますね。他にも何か言われたりしますか？
dialogue.English: That must be irritating. Does she say anything else?

dialogue.content: 早く帰りなさいとか、早く起きなさいとか、早くお風呂入りなさいとか、色々言われる
dialogue.English: She tells me to come home early, wake up early, take a bath early... all sorts of things.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。あまりに毎日言われたら嫌になっちゃいますね。確認が遅くなりましたが、あなたは15歳の高校１年生でしょうか？または中学３年生ですか？
dialogue.English: I see. Hearing that every day must be getting tiresome. I should have asked earlier, but are you 15 and in your first year of high school? Or are you in your third year of middle school?

dialogue.content: 高一
dialogue.English: First year of high school.

dialogue.content: 6月で16歳
dialogue.English: I'll be 16 in June.

dialogue.content: 高校１年生なんですね。教えていただきありがとうございます。　そしてもうすぐお誕生日ですね！おめでとうございます！
dialogue.English: So you're in your first year of high school. Thank you for telling me. And your birthday is coming up soon! Congratulations!

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: お誕生日も楽しみですね！ところで、高校生になって中学時代とは生活に変化はありましたか？
dialogue.English: You must be looking forward to your birthday! By the way, has your life changed at all since you started high school, compared to your middle school days?

dialogue.content: 先生とかまわりの人とかは変わりました
dialogue.English: My teachers and the people around me have changed.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。まわりの人は変わった感じですね。あなたの生活リズムについてはいかがですか？
dialogue.English: I see. So the people around you have changed. What about your daily routine?

dialogue.content: 朝30分早く起きるようになりました
dialogue.English: I’ve started waking up 30 minutes earlier in the morning.

dialogue.content: ええ、３０分も早起きするようになったのですね！頑張っていますね。
dialogue.English: Wow, you're waking up a full 30 minutes earlier! You're working really hard.

dialogue.content: では、お母さんは高校生になってからあなたの生活態度をみていちいちうるさいのではなく以前から・・・でしょうか？
dialogue.English: So, has your mother always been nagging you about your lifestyle, or did it start after you entered high school?

dialogue.content: 最近かな
dialogue.English: Recently, I think.

dialogue.content: なるほど、最近からなんですね。それは戸惑いますね…毎日朝も早起きして新生活を頑張っているあなたにうるさく言ってくるようになった、、何か理由は思い浮かびますか？
dialogue.English: I see, so this is a recent thing. That must be confusing... You're working hard, waking up early every day for your new school life, and now she's started nagging you. Can you think of any reason why?

dialogue.content: あると言えばあるかも、、、
dialogue.English: Well, there might be something...

dialogue.content: ええ、あるのですね。もしよければ教えていただけますか？言える範囲で結構ですので。
dialogue.English: I see, there might be. If you’re comfortable, could you tell me about it? Just as much as you feel able to share.

dialogue.content: 彼氏がいるのがバレた事かな
dialogue.English: Maybe because she found out I have a boyfriend.

dialogue.content: なるほど！そうなんですね。それはお母さんも親心から心配されているのかもしれないですね。とはいえ、毎日いちいち、しかもあれこれ言われたらいやですよね。
dialogue.English: I see! So that's what it is. It might be that your mother is worried about you, out of parental concern. Still, being nagged every day about every little thing must be unpleasant.

dialogue.content: あなたはこの先どんな風になっていったらいいな、と思われますか？
dialogue.English: How would you like things to be going forward?

dialogue.content: まだ分かりません
dialogue.English: I don't know yet.

dialogue.content: うるさく言わないでほしい
dialogue.English: I just want her to stop nagging me.

dialogue.content: ええ、そうなんですね。どうなったらいいか分からないけど、今の現状は嫌だし、うるさく言わないで欲しい…
dialogue.English: Right, I understand. You're not sure how you want things to be, but you know you don't like the current situation and you want her to stop nagging...

dialogue.content: そんな風にお思いということでよろしいでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Is that a fair summary of how you're feeling?

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: お答えいただきありがとうございます。今日は嫌な気分を抱えながらも、こうして勇気を出してお話ししに来てくれました。
dialogue.English: Thank you for answering. Even though you're feeling upset, you've shown a lot of courage by coming here to talk about it today.

dialogue.content: ぜひ一緒にどんなことができるか考えさせてくださいね。
dialogue.English: Please, let's think together about what we can do.

dialogue.content: うるさく言わないで欲しい…ということでしたが、お母さんが一番言ってくることは、どんなことでしょうか？
dialogue.English: You mentioned you want her to stop nagging... What is the thing she nags you about the most?

dialogue.content: 勉強しなさい、遊んでばかりはダメと言われる
dialogue.English: She tells me to study, and that I shouldn't just be having fun all the time.

dialogue.content: なるほど、そうなんですね。勉強について言われるのですね。。遊んでばかりはダメと・・・
dialogue.English: I see, so it's about studying... And that you shouldn't just be having fun...

dialogue.content: 実際のところ、あなたは勉強はご自分なりにはどうですか？やっている？やってないと感じますか？？
dialogue.English: In reality, how do you feel about your studying? Do you feel you are studying, or not so much?

dialogue.content: 予備校も行ってるし、４月のテストも良かったし
dialogue.English: I'm going to a cram school, and my test in April went well.

dialogue.content: まぁ、そうなんですね！予備校にも通っていらっしゃり、４月のテストも良かった。とても頑張っていらっしゃいますね。
dialogue.English: Oh, that's wonderful! You're attending a cram school, and your April test went well. You're working very hard.

dialogue.content: その点については、お母さんはどう言っているのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: What does your mother say about that?

dialogue.content: いつどうなるかわからないから、勉強しろって言う
dialogue.English: She says, 'You never know what might happen, so study.'

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。ええ、そうなんですね。お母さんはどうなるか分からないから、もっと勉強しろと…今すでに頑張っていることを認めてもらえないとしんどくなりますよね。。
dialogue.English: I see. Yes, I see. Your mother says you have to study more because you never know what might happen... It must be tough when your current efforts aren't being acknowledged.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: そうですよね・・・ちなみに、お母さんはどんな進路にして欲しくて、あなたにもっと勉強して欲しいなどと、勉強する具体的な理由などはお話しをされたことはありますか？
dialogue.English: Right… By the way, has your mother ever talked about what path she hopes you’ll take, or given any specific reasons for wanting you to study more?

dialogue.content: そういうのはないです。お母さんは、自分が高卒だから、私に頭良くなってほしいだけだと思います
dialogue.English: No, nothing like that. I think it's because she only graduated high school, so she wants me to be smart.

dialogue.content: そうですか。そして、そうお感じなのですね。お母さんはあなたに頭が良くなって欲しいとお思いの可能性が高い…
dialogue.English: I see—that’s how it feels to you. It’s likely your mother wants you to become more academically capable…

dialogue.content: お母さんの想いは大いにあると思いますが、漠然と期待を押し付けられてもつらいこもしれないですね・・・
dialogue.English: I'm sure your mother has strong feelings about this, but having such vague expectations pushed on you can be difficult...

dialogue.content: お母さんはもっと頑張って欲しい、でもあなたは現状は頑張っている、そこの認識の違いを二人でお話しされたら今よりは少しでも口うるささが減るかな？と思ったのですが、いかがでしょうか？？
dialogue.English: Your mother wants you to try harder, but you feel you are already trying hard. I was thinking that if the two of you could talk about this difference in perception, perhaps the nagging might lessen a little. What do you think?

dialogue.content: 良ければお母さんとしっかりお話しすることは出来たりしようですか？
dialogue.English: If you're up for it, would it be possible to have a proper talk with your mother?

dialogue.content: （失礼しました。しそうですか？　です）
dialogue.English: (My apologies. I meant to ask, 'does it seem possible?')

dialogue.content: 話しましたが、気になってしまうらしく、ケンカになります
dialogue.English: I've tried talking to her, but she seems to get worked up, and it turns into a fight.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。すでにお話しされていたのですね。状況を変えようと自ら行動されていることは素晴らしいと思います。しかし、ケンカになると・・・
dialogue.English: I see. So you've already tried talking. It's wonderful that you're taking action yourself to change the situation. But it ends in a fight...

dialogue.content: 話し合いで喧嘩になった、そのような時はどこでお話しをされたかおぼえていますか？
dialogue.English: When you had that talk that turned into a fight, do you remember where you were talking?

dialogue.content: 自宅で話しました
dialogue.English: We talked at home.

dialogue.content: ご自宅ですね。お母さんとあなたの二人でですか？それとも他にも誰かいましたか？？
dialogue.English: At home, I see. Was it just the two of you? Or was anyone else there?

dialogue.content: 2人です
dialogue.English: Just the two of us.

dialogue.content: お二人ですね。教えていただきありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Just the two of you. Thank you for telling me.

dialogue.content: 自宅で、当事者のみでお話しするとついつい喧嘩になりがちですよね…そこでもしよければですが、
dialogue.English: It's easy for things to turn into a fight when you're talking at home with just the two people involved... So, if you're open to it,

dialogue.content: 状況改善に向けて、またあなたの想いもお母さんに分かってもらうために今度は自宅以外の場所で、話し合ってみたはどうかと思ったのですがいかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: to help improve the situation and to help your mother understand your feelings, I was wondering what you think about trying to talk somewhere other than home next time?

dialogue.content: 例えば、お互いの好きなメニューがあるカフェやレストランなど、少し冷静になれる人の目がある場所はおススメですがいかがですか？？
dialogue.English: For example, a cafe or restaurant that has food you both like—a place where other people are around might help you both stay a bit calmer. I'd recommend it, but what do you think?

dialogue.content: それも良いかもしれませんね
dialogue.English: That might be a good idea.

dialogue.content: 最近お母さんには、頭が来ているので、話したくないのにうるさい
dialogue.English: Lately, I've been so angry with my mom. I don't want to talk, but she keeps nagging.

dialogue.content: ええ、そうなのですね…頭に来ているから話したくない。そう思っても当然ですね、、
dialogue.English: Yes, I see... You're angry, so you don't want to talk. It's perfectly natural to feel that way.

dialogue.content: みんなの前で殴りたい
dialogue.English: I want to hit her in front of everyone.

dialogue.content: 殴ってスッキリするなら、親でも良いと思う
dialogue.English: If hitting her would make me feel better, I think it's fine even if she's my parent.

dialogue.content: なのにうるさく話しかけてくる…殴りたいくらい頭にきているのですね、、それもあなたの大切な感情ですが、
dialogue.English: And yet she keeps nagging you... You're so angry you feel like hitting her. That's a valid and important feeling you're having, but...

dialogue.content: ええ、そうお感じなのですね。ただ実際に殴ってしまうと、取り返しのつかないことになることもあるので、殴らずに状況改善に向かう方法を試してみるのはいかがですか？
dialogue.English: Yes, I understand that's how you feel. However, actually hitting someone can have irreversible consequences, so how about we try to find a way to improve the situation without resorting to violence?

dialogue.content: それぐらい嫌だと言う気持ちを是非お母さんに伝えてみるのはどうでしょうか？
dialogue.English: How about trying to convey to your mother just how much you dislike this?

dialogue.content: お母さんは、私に暴力したよ
dialogue.English: My mom was violent with me.

dialogue.content: 過去に暴力をしたことがあるのですね。例えば殴ったや蹴ったとかでしょうか？？その時お母さんのご様子はどうでしたか？
dialogue.English: She has been violent with you in the past? For example, did she hit or kick you? What was your mother's demeanor like at the time?

dialogue.content: あっ、失礼しました。
dialogue.English: Ah, my apologies.

dialogue.content: 読み違いですね。大変申し訳ございません。
dialogue.English: I misread that. I am very sorry.

dialogue.content: お母さんが暴力を・・・
dialogue.English: Your mother used violence…

dialogue.content: 昨日初めてぶたれた
dialogue.English: She hit me for the first time yesterday.

dialogue.content: 許せない
dialogue.English: I can't forgive her.

dialogue.content: なるほど、、昨日。それはそう思いますね。。痛かったと思います。つらいですよね・・・
dialogue.English: I see... Yesterday. I can certainly understand why you'd feel that way. It must have hurt. That's so painful...

dialogue.content: うるさいだけでなく、昨日ぶたれた。泣きたいです
dialogue.English: It's not just the nagging, she hit me yesterday. I want to cry.

dialogue.content: そうですよね、、もっともな気持ちです。。大変でしたね…親とはいえ、暴力はやってはいけないことです。続く場合は公的機関、警察や児童相談所に通報も視野に入れなければ、と思いますが、昨日初めて、ということなのでよければ、あなたのその気持ちを是非お母さんに伝えていただきたいと思いますがいかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Of course... those are completely valid feelings. That must have been awful... Even if she's your parent, violence is never okay. If it continues, we'll have to consider reporting it to public agencies like the police or child protective services. But since this was the first time, if you're willing, I'd really encourage you to tell your mother how you feel. What do you think?

dialogue.content: 話したくないなら、書く　でもいいと思います。
dialogue.English: If you don't want to talk, writing it down is also an option.

dialogue.content: 今朝流石に謝ってきたけど、私は許せない
dialogue.English: She did apologize this morning, but I can't forgive her.

dialogue.content: もうどうしようもない
dialogue.English: It feels hopeless.

dialogue.content: 謝ってくれたのですね、それでも許せない…どうしようもないというお気持ちも当然だと思います。
dialogue.English: So she apologized, but you still can't forgive her... It's completely understandable to feel like the situation is hopeless.

dialogue.content: 今、あなた自身が行動に移せない場合は、他のご家族や先生など、第三者に介入してもらう・・・ということも有効かと思いますがいかがですか？
dialogue.English: If you don't feel you can take action yourself right now, it might be effective to have a third party intervene, like another family member or a teacher. What do you think about that?

dialogue.content: まだ頭が混乱してます
dialogue.English: My head is still a mess.

dialogue.content: そうですよね、、今は混乱していて当然です。そろそろ終了のお時間となってしまい今日はここまでとなりすが、どうでしょう、少し落ち着いたら紙に書いたり、誰か他の人をたよったり、何かできそうでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Of course... it's only natural to be confused right now. Our time is almost up, so we'll have to stop here for today. But how about this: once you've calmed down a little, do you think you might be able to try something, like writing things down or reaching out to someone else?

dialogue.content: 何かしたら、行動をしたいです。まだ高校始まって、やっと彼氏と幸せになるって決めたのに
dialogue.English: I want to do something, take some kind of action. High school just started, and I had just decided I was finally going to be happy with my boyfriend.

dialogue.content: そうですね！前向きに思えるあなたならきっと乗り越えていけると思います。つらい中、お話しに来てくださったあなたを応援していますので、また是非いつでもお話しに来ていただけたらと思います。これで終了となります。本日はありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: That's right! Someone as forward-thinking as you can definitely get through this. I'm rooting for you for coming to talk today even when things are so tough. Please feel free to come back and talk anytime. This concludes our session. Thank you for your time today.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: こちらこそありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you as well.

dialogue.content: （お疲れ様でした）
dialogue.English: (Thank you for your time.)

dialogue.content: （最後きちんとまとまらず失礼いたしました。大変勉強になりました。ありがとうございました！！）
dialogue.English: (I apologize that we couldn't come to a clear conclusion at the end. This was a great learning experience for me. Thank you very much!)
